Approach slopes.notes: From the high camp, cross beneath the steep southwest buttress in the dark and climb a long, uniform snow slope of 30-40 degrees, gaining nearly 1,500 ft. It ends at the first bergschrund, around 7,600 ft.

Bergschrund/serac crux.notes: A serac about 50 ft high guards the way over the first bergschrund. The line goes straight up its face on 70-85 degree snow, starting from a small snow bridge over the crack. A fall here lands in the schrund; the snow is kick-stepped.

Steep gullies.notes: Above the serac, 45-50 degree slopes lead left toward a rock island, then a traverse into a hidden gully of about 60 degrees. Deep runnels, 4-5 ft wide, are the hardest part. A second schrund is usually snow-covered and easy. The final gully eases to about 50 degrees and ends in bare rock.

Snow arete.notes: A longer, narrow snow crest with steep drop-offs on both sides, reached from the upper gully. A leftward traverse along the moat against the rock follows, and one more big runnel is the only other difficulty before the last gully.
